originalTitle: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
content: The New York Times is asking freelance photographers not to use the newest version of Adobe Photoshop because features in the 2027 update use AI “in ways that may not be apparent to users.” In an email seen by The Verge and posted on Threads, two of the Times’ photography leaders, Meaghan Looram and Josh Haner, write that the use of these features “can result in metadata identifying photographs as AI-generated.” Adobe has spent the past few years filling Photoshop and other apps in its creative suite with a trove of AI-powered tools. The November update cited by the NYT’s email adds several new AI features, including Adobe’s new “AI Assisted Editor” view, which lets users access all of Photoshop’s AI features from a single toolbar. It also adds an AI assistant for step-by-step editing instructions, prompt-based image transformation and editing, new AI upscaling options, and an AI-powered tool that recomposes images for different canvas sizes. [Media: https://www.threads.com/@peterbaker/post/DgHHIz1FRpO] It’s not always clear which tools in Adobe’s apps are AI-powered, and even some older options like automated selection tools may now be considered part of the AI suite. This can lead to photos ending up with metadata indicating they were edited with AI, which is a blunt way of describing what happened in post-production. For a newsroom like the Times, where photo editing is kept to a minimum, the metadata risks losing readers’ trust. Last year, the Times said that it does not “retouch or digitally manipulate” photos but may “make minimal adjustments to color to ensure we are accurately reproducing the image.” In August, Adobe began rolling out support for C2PA metadata across its apps, which indicates whether an image is AI-generated or edited using AI features. The NYT is issuing its restriction to keep these tags from inadvertently appearing in its photos. “At this time, we are requiring that all contributing photographers avoid using Adobe Photoshop 2027 (release 28.0.0 and subsequent updates) when working on assignment for The Times,” the email reads. NYT spokesperson Graham James confirmed the requirement in a statement to The Verge, which reiterated the policy outlined in the email. It’s still not clear which specific Photoshop features the NYT is referring to. Adobe didn’t immediately respond to The Verge’s request for more information. Update, November 24th: Added confirmation from the NYT.
chineseTitle: 《纽约时报》警告摄影师不要因为 AI 功能而更新 Photoshop
chineseContent: 《纽约时报》要求自由摄影师不要使用最新版本的 Adob​​e Photoshop，因为 2027 年更新中的功能“以用户可能不明显的方式”使用人工智能。在 The Verge 看到并发布在 Threads 上的一封电子邮件中，《纽约时报》的两位摄影领袖 Meaghan Looram 和 Josh Haner 写道，使用这些功能“可以导致元数据将照片识别为人工智能生成的”。 Adobe 在过去的几年里一直在其创意套件中使用大量人工智能工具填充 Photoshop 和其他应用程序。 《纽约时报》电子邮件引用的 11 月更新添加了多项新的 AI 功能，包括 Adob​​e 新的“AI 辅助编辑器”视图，该视图允许用户从单个工具栏访问 Photoshop 的所有 AI 功能。它还添加了一个人工智能助手，用于分步编辑指令、基于提示的图像转换和编辑、新的人工智能升级选项，以及一个人工智能驱动的工具，可以根据不同的画布尺寸重新组合图像。 [媒体：https://www.threads.com/@peterbaker/post/DgHHIz1FRpO] Adob​​e 应用程序中的哪些工具是由 AI 驱动的并不总是很清楚，甚至一些较旧的选项（例如自动选择工具）现在也可能被视为 AI 套件的一部分。这可能会导致照片最终带有元数据，表明它们是用人工智能编辑的，这是描述后期制作中发生的情况的一种直白方式。对于像《纽约时报》这样的新闻编辑室来说，照片编辑被保持在最低限度，元数据可能会失去读者的信任。去年，《纽约时报》表示，它不会“修饰或数字化处理”照片，但可能“对颜色进行最小程度的调整，以确保我们准确地再现图像。” 8 月，Adobe 开始在其应用程序中推出对 C2PA 元数据的支持，该元数据表明图像是 AI 生成的还是使用 AI 功能编辑的。纽约时报
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于 AI 与科技趋势信号，适合用于观察工具选型、产品机会、开发者关注点和技术路线变化。
